title: Software Solution for N2 Diversion in δ18O Measurement of Nitrogen-Rich Samples
author: Brodie

steps.title: Create CO method in Isodat
steps.instruction: Open the Acquisition or Workspace module of Isodat, click “New” → “Method”. In the Method window set Gas Configuration to “CO”, Auto Dilution to “Fixed”, and enter values for Reference Intensity (mV) and Sample Dilution (%).

substeps.instruction: Open Isodat and select New → Method.
Enter Reference Intensity (mV) and Sample Dilution (%).

steps.title: Match reference and sample peak intensity
steps.instruction: Adjust the reference intensity and sample dilution so that the reference peak and sample peak are within 500 mV of each other; keep the overall signal in the 5–8 V range for reliable δ¹⁸O measurement on CO.

steps.title: Create time‑events list for N₂ diversion
steps.instruction: Using Figure 5 as a template, build the time‑events list in Isodat. If the GC column differs from the 1.5 m × 4 mm, 45‑60 mesh 5 Å molecular sieve column described, first examine a chromatogram (or a non‑diversion run) to locate where the N₂ and CO baselines resolve and adjust the timing accordingly.

steps.title: Configure remaining method tabs and save
steps.instruction: In the same Method window keep the default values in the “Compound Names”, “Evaluation@CO”, “Peak Detection@CO” and “Printout@CO” tabs unless laboratory‑specific values are required. Save the method file with an appropriate name (e.g., N2_Diversion_O_Isotopes.met).

steps.title: Create EA method file
steps.instruction: In the Isodat Acquisition module create an EA method using the parameters in Table 1 for a Flash 2000/EA IsoLink or Table 2 for a TC/EA. Enter all instrument settings exactly as listed.

substeps.instruction: • Helium Carrier Pressure Regulator = 0.4 kPa (40 ml/min)
• Helium Reference Pressure Regulator = 1.1 kPa (100 ml/min)
Enter GC column description: 1.5 m length, 4 mm inner diameter, packed with 45‑60 mesh 5 Å molecular sieve.

steps.title: Verify flow and configure ConFlo IV
steps.instruction: Place the ConFlo IV device in Standby mode, attach a flow meter to the exit capillary, and confirm that the measured carrier flow matches the expected values (≈40 ml/min carrier, 100 ml/min reference). Ensure the Sample Open Split timing (2 s – 305 s) and capillary switches at 305 s are programmed as shown in Figures 5‑7.

substeps.instruction: Set ConFlo IV to Standby to avoid atmospheric air ingress.
Connect flow meter to the exit capillary (ConFlo IV output).
Check carrier flow ≈40 ml/min and reference flow ≈100 ml/min.
Program Sample Open Split: LF‑On & MS Capillary‑On at 2 s, HF Capillary‑On & HF II‑On at 8 s (Fig. 6).
Program capillary switch at 305 s so that HF and MS capillaries change position and CO is delivered to the mass spectrometer (Fig. 7).

steps.title: Create sequence file
steps.instruction: In the Acquisition or Workspace module select “New” → “Sequence”. Choose the number of samples, enter sample type, amount and any other metadata, then assign the EA method and the CO time‑events method created earlier. Save the sequence file according to local laboratory conventions.

substeps.instruction: Select number of samples to analyse.
Enter sample type, mass, and other required metadata.
Link the EA method file and the CO time‑events method.
Save the sequence file with an appropriate name.

steps.title: Monitor CO peak and maintain column
steps.instruction: During analysis record the CO peak retention time, peak width and intensity. If the peak widens, intensity drops, or retention time shifts later, bake the GC column as needed and inspect reactor and capillary lines for blockages.
